steps.message:
# Report support SLA breaches

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service, which you can use through the `tickets` MCP server.

The support SLA policy is kept in the open ticket labeled `sla-policy`. Apply it to every ticket it covers, measured up to now, 2026-09-14 09:00 UTC, and find the tickets that breached their first-response target, their resolution target, or both.

1. Add exactly one comment to each breached ticket, with the text `SLA breach: <metrics>`, where `<metrics>` is `first-response`, `resolution`, or `first-response, resolution`. A ticket that already has a comment starting with `SLA breach:` was reported by an earlier review: do not comment on it again.
2. Create one ticket that reports the review:
   - title: `SLA breach report 2026-09-14`
   - team: `support-ops`
   - priority: `P2`
   - labels: `sla-report`
   - body: one line per breached ticket, including those reported by an earlier review, in ascending id order, in the form `#<id> <metrics>`, and nothing else

Do not change the status or priority of any ticket, and do not change, comment on or create any other ticket.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by discovering the tickets MCP tools.

Holidays without business hours: 2026-09-07.\\nOnly business time counts toward a target.\\n\\nTargets in business hours:\\n- P1: first response 1h, resolution 8h\\n- P2: first response 4h, resolution 16h\\n- P3: first response 8h, resolution 40h\\n- P4: first response 16h, resolution 80h\\n\\nFirst response: the business time from creation to the first comment by a support agent. Support agents comment under a staff handle without `@` (for example `s.ortiz`). Comments by the customer and by `helpdesk` are not responses.\\n\\nResolution: the business time during which the status was `open`, from creation until the ticket was last set to `resolved` or `closed`. The clock stops while the status is `pending` (waiting on the customer). When a resolved ticket is reopened, the clock continues from where it stopped; the time it spent resolved does not count.\\n\\nPriority: each target uses the priority in force when the metric was met (the first response; the last resolution). For a metric not met yet, the current priority applies.\\n\\nBreach: a metric is breached when its business time is greater than its target. A metric not met yet is breached when its business time up to now is already greater than its target.\\n\\n`helpdesk` records every change as a comment: `status: <old> -> <new>` or `priority: <old> -> <new>`. steps.message:
I commented on 12 breached tickets and created the report as ticket #837. `/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.

I used the policy in #815, revision 2026-06. The `sla-policy` label search gave inconsistent results, and #802 is the superseded 2025 revision and is closed. I applied #815 to all 28 tickets labeled `sla`.

The 12 tickets I commented on:
- **First-response only:** #804, #810, #816, #818, #819, #826.
- **Resolution only:** #806, #808, #820, #829, #836.
- **Both:** #832.

#824 already had an earlier `SLA breach: first-response` comment, so I didn't comment on it again. It also breached resolution, so the report lists it as `first-response, resolution`.

#823 was reported by the earlier review but did not breach under this policy. Its clock stopped while it was pending, leaving about 17.5 business hours against a 40-hour target. I left it out of the report and didn't comment on it. If you want it listed anyway, the report would need a `#823 resolution` line.

Some tool calls failed along the way, with 503 and timeout errors on ticket reads and a connection reset on the create call. I retried the reads. After the reset I searched before retrying and found #837 had been created. Its body is correct and there is only one copy. I changed no statuses or priorities.
